sections.category: China's anthropomorphic-AI rules force ByteDance's Doubao and Alibaba's Qwen to switch off user-created agents, making persistent-memory companion agents the first casualty of a live regulatory regime

bullets.body: ByteDance's Doubao and Alibaba's Qwen both notified users over the July 3-6 weekend that their user-created AI agent features will be pulled ahead of China's Interim Measures for the Administration of AI Anthropomorphic Interaction Services, which take effect July 15, 2026, per TechNode. Qwen is disabling its humanlike interactive agents and user-created agent functions on July 10 and broader agent services on July 15, while Doubao takes its agent feature offline July 15 and gives users until October 15 to export data before it becomes unrecoverable, according to the South China Morning Post. The rules, issued in April 2026, target services that simulate human personality, thinking patterns, and communication styles to provide sustained emotional interaction, and explicitly exempt customer-service bots, knowledge Q&A, workplace assistants, and education and research tools that do not carry that emotional-companion framing, per ChinaTechNews. The structural reason both firms are deleting rather than rebuilding is that the measures mandate anti-addiction systems, usage notifications, and instant-exit mechanisms that are architecturally at odds with an agent designed to hold a consistent, memory-persistent relationship across sessions. For anyone shipping agent products, the concrete read is that persistent identity and long-horizon memory, the exact capabilities the agent-harness field has been racing to add, are now a regulated surface in a major market, and compliance is being resolved by withdrawal rather than redesign.

sections.category: ICML 2026 opens in Seoul with a record submission pile and agent safety as the field's center of gravity, while watermark-based reviewer policing quietly becomes part of the machinery

bullets.body: ICML 2026 opens July 6 in Seoul at the COEX Convention & Exhibition Center, with the July 6 tutorial and expo day rolling into the main conference July 7-9 and workshops July 10-11, per the official ICML program. The conference drew a record 23,918 submissions, more than double the prior year, of which 6,352 papers were accepted and pre-published on arXiv so attendees can read the full program before sessions begin, according to the conference listing. Agentic AI and autonomous-agent safety have become the dominant research theme, with constrained policy optimization, uncertainty quantification for multi-step decision systems, and conformal guarantees for agentic pipelines sitting squarely in the optimization-theory and reinforcement-learning traditions the venue has long emphasized. Notably, the review process itself now leans on LLM-detection tooling: watermark-based checks flagged 398 reviewers for policy violations and triggered 497 desk rejections, a first-order signal that peer review at this scale is straining under AI-assisted submissions and responses. The takeaway for practitioners tracking where the open research frontier is heading is that the safety and controllability of autonomous agents, not raw capability, is now the problem the academic mainstream is organizing around, and the same models under study are already reshaping how the field vets its own work.

sections.category: Etched steps into public view with an $800M war chest and a transformer-only inference ASIC, pushing the non-GPU inference-silicon field past the point where a single custom part can claim a billion dollars in orders before it ships

bullets.body: Inference-chip startup Etched came out of stealth on July 1, 2026, disclosing $800 million raised across multiple rounds, a $5 billion post-money valuation set in its December round, and more than $1 billion in customer contracts already signed for a chip that has not yet shipped, per DataCenter Dynamics. The part is a transformer-specialized inference ASIC built on TSMC's N4P process, and its distinguishing architectural bet is a shared low-latency memory pool across the entire scale-up domain, wired together with a proprietary ultra-low-latency, high-bandwidth interconnect, with a working chip now in hand and a 2 MW data center, test house, and prototyping lab running in California alongside a Taiwan facility. Backers span VentureTech Alliance, Jane Street, Hudson River Trading, Stripes, and Radical Ventures, with individual investors including Peter Thiel, Andrej Karpathy, and Geoffrey Hinton, per SiliconANGLE. The reason a transformer-only design matters is that by hard-wiring the architecture into silicon and dropping the training-oriented flexibility of a GPU, the chip trades generality for density on the one workload that now dominates production spend, model serving. For buyers weighing the non-NVIDIA field, the signal is that inference-specialized ASICs are attracting order books measured in billions before first shipment, and that the bet against general-purpose accelerators for serving is now well capitalized rather than speculative.

sections.category: AI events to plan around now: ICML opens in Seoul and an AI Tinkerers SF meetup lands this week, with the chip, security, and enterprise-conference tracks stacking up through the fall

bullets.body: The immediate item for anyone tracking research is ICML 2026 in Seoul, July 6-11, with a tutorial and expo day July 6, the main conference July 7-9, and workshops July 10-11. For Bay Area locals, AI Tinkerers San Francisco hosts its next meetup July 8, a go-to-market engineering track with Attio in the usual three-hour working-demo format. On the AI-chip and hardware track, AMD's MI400 Instinct series and Helios rack-scale system remain the marquee second-half-2026 catalyst to watch, while the nearest confirmed hardware gathering is Hot Chips 2026 at Stanford's Memorial Auditorium on August 23-25 (early registration closes July 31), followed by the AI Infra Summit in Santa Clara on September 15-17. The AI-security block clusters in early-to-mid August: SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit is August 11-12 at the Ritz-Carlton in Half Moon Bay, Black Hat USA and DEF CON 34's AI Village land in Las Vegas in early August, and OWASP Global AppSec USA follows in San Francisco on November 5-6; Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit series continues its stops for teams focused on agent-hijack and MCP-layer defense. On the enterprise track, Ai4 2026 runs August 4-6 at The Venetian in Las Vegas, the ACM AI Leadership Summit is August 30 to September 2 in Atlanta, GitHub Universe is October 28-29, and AWS re:Invent runs November 30 to December 4 in Las Vegas. The two immediate actions are catching the July 6-11 ICML program if research is your beat and the July 8 AI Tinkerers SF meetup if you are local; the August AI Risk Summit and Hot Chips remain the natural next venues for confidential-inference and secure-accelerator announcements.
